notes:
Independent review by Claude Code, session cc-7b31c4, issue #1227, 23 September 2026, of the extraction by Claude Code, session cc-442dc5 (issue #1226). Sources read: arXiv:2203.09490v3 in both forms the extraction records, and both hashes reproduce byte for byte — the PDF 3c49a5f2aa6023c7b01a5ba83a370ddcb92642f4819f64446b7d93bf01b28d26 (111 pages) and the LaTeX e-print 039db4d2567289b85425fac4806d7550585b55c6f4a7cba23fdace13ee55fb36 (main.tex, 5372 lines, and main.bbl). Because the e-print is the authors' own source, every check below was made against the LaTeX rather than against an extracted text layer, and the verdicts cite TeX line numbers. v3 is the current arXiv version; Crossref carries no update-to, updated-by or other correction relation for DOI 10.1007/s00222-024-01238-4, and the published Inventiones text is paywalled and was not compared, as the extraction states.

Verdict: accept, all nine routes accepted, nothing rejected.

Findings. All 35 recorded sourceIssues now carry verdicts and all 35 are confirmed: 23 misprints, 6 errors and 6 gaps. The three that matter for the mathematics are E12 (Proposition 3.7 is false under the standing quasi-syntomic hypothesis of §3 — for X = Spf k the unit has endomorphisms Z_p on one side and Q_p on the other — and needs X flat over O_K), E10 (Proposition 2.29 and Corollaries 2.30, 2.35 are false without quasi-compactness, since inverting p does not commute with infinite products) and E17, which I verified in the cited source: Shiho, arXiv:0707.1742, fixes a base log formal scheme separated and topologically of finite type over Spf W ('Note that B is Noetherian'), while Corollary 6.14 applies Theorem 6.13(ii) at A_crys(S), which is neither. E14 is a genuine error of the same kind — no ring map R -> Delta_S exists over ramified K, by an Eisenstein argument in the p-torsionfree W(S^flat) — and E9 shows that the printed invariant computation in the proof of Proposition 2.29 produces the K-algebra where the K_0-algebra is wanted. None of these overturns a main theorem, and the extraction's corrections are right in each case.

One finding added (E36, misprint, Construction 10.6(2)): the de Rham complex displayed there ends at Omega^d_{Z/Y_K}, but d is fixed by Convention 10.4 as the relative dimension of X over Y while the complex is that of Z, which has relative dimension |Sigma| in the framed case the construction goes on to use. The extraction had noticed the exponent and left it unrecorded.

Corrections made in place. The extraction attached to eight items a note of the form 'Possible misprint noted during reading, not verified and not recorded in sourceIssues: (...)'. In two of those eight the parenthetical is recorded in sourceIssues (items 253 and 254 are E33 and E34), in one it duplicates a note that already cites E8 (item 070), in one it is not a misprint claim at all (item 258), and in one it is the finding now added as E36 (item 246); the remaining three (items 247, 248, 249) are notational points about Theorem 10.7. I rewrote all eight notes to say what is true of each: cross-references where a finding exists, and, for the three notational points, the reason they are not mistakes — in particular the 'degeneracy map [a] -> [0]' of Theorem 10.7(ii) induces the diagonal, while the isomorphism asserted is the one induced by the projections Z^{a+1} -> Z, which is what the proof uses and which is its inverse.

Structure, verified in full. 274 items (220 missing, 52 planned, 2 library) and nine routes: two Part IIs, one further Part II and one new roadmap that join proposals the corpus already carries, and five source routes. Every missing item is routed exactly once and no routed id is unknown or non-missing. All nine route stage ids resolve in data/atlas.json, layer-level ids included (RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0:integral-Y and RF4:vector-bundles). All 38 distinct planned references resolve: 36 of Stage or Stage:Layer form in data/atlas.json, and two of the corpus-wide tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/...#layer-... form whose targets live in the Tau Ceti repository. All three Part II titles reproduce their parents' atlas titles exactly, all four declared areas are galaxy ids, and all four proposed roadmap ids are free in data/atlas.json. Both library citations resolve at the pinned commits recorded in `baseline`: mathlib:OrzechProperty is the class at Mathlib/RingTheory/OrzechProperty.lean:63 (whose consequence injective_of_surjective_endomorphism at line 101 is the statement the item names, supplied for commutative rings by instance (priority := 100) CommRing.orzechProperty at Mathlib/RingTheory/FiniteType.lean:625) and mathlib:associatedPrimes is at Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/AssociatedPrime/Basic.lean:103, with finiteness over noetherian rings at AssociatedPrime/Finiteness.lean:158. No libraryPins block was added because `baseline` already records both commits.

Coverage. I extracted every numbered environment from the LaTeX: 192, under one counter numbered by section plus the lettered main results. 167 of them are named in item locators or names. The 25 that are not are 18 remarks, one example and six statements of the introduction (Theorems 1.10, 1.13, 1.18, 1.21 and Corollary 1.23) that restate body results, each of which is itemised at its body number (6.1, 6.4, 6.8; 7.8, 7.16; 8.1; 9.1; 9.15). So every result of the paper is carried.

One cross-extraction inconsistency, left for the design job. SchemeAndStackFoundationsMixedCharacteristicBirationalGeometry is proposed with area algebraicgeometry here and by PAPER-HACON-WITASZEK-23, and with area arithmeticgeometry by PAPER-BHATT-ETAL-23. Both are galaxy ids and one roadmap cannot sit in two galaxies; this extraction is with the majority, so I changed nothing.

Two printed slips are recorded by no finding and I leave them rather than manufacture findings: the displayed definition of the de Rham complex in Construction 10.6(2) has a misplaced parenthesis (dR(F_{D_Z(X)} := (F_{D_Z(X)}) -> ...), and the sentence closing Example 1.8 refers to O_{Y_[0,infty)} where the example's own item (2) puts M(T) over Y_[0,1/p].

What this review did not do. I did not re-derive the paper's proofs. I read the introduction and the list of period rings in full, the statements the routes cite, every passage a finding names together with the surrounding argument, and the sections needed to judge them (§§2.2–2.4, 3, 4.2, 5.3, 6, 7, 8, 9.1, 10). I did not compare the published Inventiones text, so no finding here is checked against the version of record. scripts/check_paper.py and research/blueprint/intake.py check-files both pass.
